acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/design/req185-scheduler-firing-architecture.md exists and names exactly ONE recommended firing mechanism, with the alternatives it rejected and the reason for each -- evaluating at minimum Oban, a supervised GenServer ticker, and a per-timer process

the artefact states an explicit YES or NO on adopting Oban as a mix.exs dependency, with REVIEWER sign-off recorded in the artefact; it does not leave the choice open or defer it to the implementing requirement

the artefact names FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (or its chosen alternative) as the claim mechanism and states in its own text that R-Co REMOVED the per-timer advisory lock SCH-02's literal text mandates, citing src/design/scheduler-concurrency-epic3.md's ISS-301 section, so a later reader does not reintroduce it

the artefact decides whether an equivalent of R-Co's ISS-302 session-level startup-sweep lock is needed in Letflow, and if not, states what prevents two nodes both sweeping overdue timers on simultaneous restart

the artefact states how the poller relates to Letflow's per-tenant schemas -- whether it iterates tenant schemas per tick or polls one global queue -- and quantifies the cost of the chosen strategy at a stated tenant count, rather than describing it qualitatively

the artefact states, in one section, how the recommended design distinguishes 'timer locked by another node', 'no timer due' and 'hard non-retryable error' from each other, citing src/design/iss0618-scheduler-lock-and-error-signaling.md, and states why simply propagating every error out of the fire path is the WRONG fix (it stops the poll loop before fire_error_count can reach its limit)
the artefact decides whether an exhausted-retry timer lands in REQ-176's dlq_entries with entry_type "timer", answering yes or no rather than leaving it to REQ-186
